re_salt_wind.text: A wind comes off the pans with salt in it, and for an hour the world is a white hiss and the track is a guess. You walk bent, with your sleeve over your mouth, and come out of it with your eyes raw and the sun somewhere else.

re_kite.text: Something crosses the sun with no bird in it: long wings, no beat, a shadow that slides over the salt and over you and does not hurry. It looks at you. You are fairly sure of that. Then it is a line, and then nothing.

re_dust_devil.text: A dust devil walks the pan a hundred yards off, tall as a tower, taking its time. Grit in your teeth for a mile after.

re_old_camp.text: A ring of stones by the track, and in it the ash of a fire nobody has lit for years, and a tin cup with a bullet hole through it, set upright on a rock as if someone meant to come back for it.

re_rc_wreck.text: In the ditch beside the Line, a sealed car on its side with the Concern's closed eye on its door, the door open and the seal's wire cut clean. Straw, and the square ghosts of crates in the dust. Nothing else in it. Nothing else touched.

re_rc_signal.text: Where an old branch leaves the Line and runs off into the grass with no rails on it, a signal still stands on its post, and still shows green, all night, for a train that has not come for ninety years. Somebody has hung a tin cup on its ladder. You leave it there.

re_rc_drovers.text: Drovers on the Line's verge with forty goats and two dogs, walking the grass between the rails and the road because nobody else wants it. They give you a strip of dried meat for a hand turning the herd off the track ahead of the seven o'clock.

re_rc_grassfire.text: A grass fire along the Line where an engine's sparks have caught the verge, a long low wall of smoke walking with the wind. You go round it the long way, with your sleeve over your mouth.

re_ds_fog.text: A sea fog comes in over the delta in the space of a breath, and the dike road becomes a yard of wet asphalt in a white room. You walk by the sound of the sea on your right hand, and twice the sound is somewhere it should not be. An hour later it lifts all at once, and you are where you meant to be, which surprises you.

re_ds_tide.text: The tide comes up over a low stretch of the old road faster than you can walk it, and for an hour you wade waist-deep along the line of posts with your pack on your head and the water pulling at your knees, toward the next rise.

re_ds_tideline.text: The tide line along the dike is a mile of plastic: bottle caps, the heads of toys, combs, a thousand coloured shards the sea has rounded like pebbles, ninety years old and as bright as the day they were made. A child's shoe with a light in its heel that has not lit since the Burn. Gulls walk on it as if it were a beach.

re_ds_roof_lamp.text: From the dike, across the bay in the fog, a light moves low over the water toward the drowned roofs off Gull Stilts: a lamp, carried in a boat, steady, rowed by someone who knows the way. It stops on the tallest roof and stays there. Out to the west, where Lean's light should be, there is nothing.

re_tm_snow.text: Snow comes down off the Teeth between one step and the next, sideways, so thick the pines go grey and then go. You walk with your hand on the rock face and count your steps, and an hour later it stops as if somebody had turned it off, and the whole mountain is white and ticking.

re_tm_cairn.text: A cairn beside the path where it crosses a scree, knee-high, and on its top stone a brass lamp tag with a number stamped in it and a name scratched under the number. Somebody came over from the Skirts and did not get further than this. Somebody else stopped to pile the stones.

re_tm_hare.text: A snow hare in a dead man's wire on the edge of the pines, the snare rusted to its stake and the hare fresh in it. Whoever set the line has not been back for a long time. You take the hare, and reset the wire, because somebody should.

re_tm_clean.text: Far up the slope, against the snow, four figures in grey moving in a line along a ridge path with the patience of people who are paid by the day: the Clean, walking the Concern's side of the mountain. They do not look down. You are fairly sure they know you are there.

re_nw_rain.text: The rain, which has been rain, becomes something heavier, a grey wall walking up the valley toward you with a sound like applause. You stand under a pine with your collar up for an hour and watch the path become a stream and the stream become a river and the river go on not caring.

re_nw_logjam.text: Where the river bends hard under a cliff, a jam of logs that got away from Sawtown's boom in some flood, piled like straw and silver with age. On the freshest of them, at the top, a butt with a crow's foot shaved half off it and a hook cut over the place, still pale.

re_nw_dredge.text: In the reeds of a backwater, a pre-war dredger the size of a house, rusted to the colour of the bank, with its bucket chain still hanging from its boom into the water; and, as you watch, the chain moves, a link, another link, turned by the current through some gear that has never been told to stop. On the bank beside it a heron stands and waits for whatever the buckets bring up.

re_nw_courier.text: A launch on the river with the city's grey pennant at its stern, and in it, under an umbrella that is losing, a man in Precinct grey with a leather case chained to his wrist. He calls across the water when he sees you: "Ashby? Is this the way to Ashby?" It is. "They're short," he calls, as if you had asked. "Eleven seasons short. There's to be an inspection." Then the current has him round the bend.

re_an_kite.text: A shadow goes over the glass ahead of you, and another, and you are flat on the crust before you have decided to be, with your face in your arms and the light off the ground coming up through your eyelids. Something turns in the sky above you, slow, patient, quartering. It takes an hour to go away. You are not sure it has.

re_an_kite_down.text: On the glass a mile off the road, a kite where it came down when its light ran out, one wing up like a hand, its lens dull. Pickers have already been at it: its belly plate is off and its board is gone. Somebody has stood a stick in the glass beside it with a rag tied on, the way you mark a grave or a find.

re_an_convoy.text: Across the glass, at walking pace, a convoy truck: pre-war, armoured, its cab empty, its lamps lit in broad day, driving a loop it was given ninety years ago. Its tyres are long gone; it runs on its rims, grinding a groove into the crust that goes all the way to the horizon and comes back. You stand and watch it go by at fifty yards. It does not know you are there. It does not know anything except the loop.

re_an_warden.text: At dusk, on the stump of a crossroads where a town was, a warden walker: two-legged, taller than a man, its plates sun-bleached to bone, standing where the junction's lights were. As the sun touches the glass it lifts its head and says, in a pleasant woman's voice, to nobody, "Curfew is now in effect. Please return to your homes." Then it waits, the way it has waited every dusk for ninety years, for somebody to go home.

re_an_storm.text: A glass storm: wind off the plateau carrying the crust's own dust, fine as flour and sharp as what it is. You get your scarf over your mouth and your back to it and wait it out in the lee of a fused car, an hour, listening to it scour the paint off the world.

re_an_feral.text: On a ridge to the south, against the sky, a hound: one of Kelso's heavy three, or one of the reserve that has walked out of its cradle with nobody to tell it not to. It stands. It watches you the whole length of the ridge. You walk the long way round, and it watches that too.

re_an_orbital.text: In a crater of its own making, half buried, the burned shell of a thing that fell out of the sky in the years after the Burn: a satellite, or a piece of one, its panels fanned and fused, a plate on its flank in a script you cannot read. Pickers have stripped most of it. In a seam they missed, you find a coil of fine wire and a scorched board.

re_ln_wagons.text: Guild wagons on the road, six of them in a line with empty beds, outriders on bikes at front and back, the half-moon on every tailboard and the drivers not talking. They are going to Openfield. One of the outriders looks at you a long time as he passes, the way a man looks at somebody he may see again tonight.

re_ln_column.text: A column of wardens on the road east out of the city, in grey, in step, two by two, a captain walking at their head with a case at his hip and his eyes on the ground. They give you the road's edge and do not look at you. At the back, a warden car on a flatbed, its windows plated, empty, waiting for somebody.

re_a3_column.text: A grey Precinct car goes by on the toll road at a steady forty, stencilled on its tailboard COLUMN — RESERVE 9 — SUPPLY: water barrels roped down under canvas, the Precinct's own, for the wardens camped at Knock, because Knock has none to sell them. The warden at the wheel lifts two fingers to you as it passes, politely, the way the sheet says the designate is to be greeted.
